summary: Iteration 18 targeted re-verification at mobile viewport 390x844, frontend only. (1) BUG FIX from iter17 VERIFIED: after E01 email check → tap email-check-account → /account renders account-scent-notice card with exact text 'Threat Scent Apollo saw 1 suspicious event in the last 30 minutes (about CommBank). An account alert now will be assessed as part of that sequence.'; then account-kind-mfa_prompt + account-provider-bank + account-initiated-no + account-run produces account-state 'Barking' AND account-linked text '• Connected to: Email: Email impersonating CommBank (Threat Scent). These events may be connected — do not approve the login request.' The fix (adding 'email' to the recentLinked whitelist in /app/frontend/app/account.tsx:66) works end-to-end. (2) GROWLING GIF NEW FEATURE VERIFIED: fresh onboarding → home-check-message-button → paste 'Hi, your parcel is waiting, pay $2.99 redelivery' → message-check → message-state 'Growling'; close back to Home → apollo-state-label reads 'Apollo is growling', apollo-hero-gif-growling testID is present (bark=False, growl=True, rest=False), ends with 'apollo-growling.gif'. (3) REGRESSION SMOKE: fresh home shows apollo-state-label 'Apollo is patrolling' + apollo-hero-gif (patrolling) testID present; /email opens (email-body input, email-run works) and closes via email-close returning to /home; /account opens (account-dashboard renders) and closes via account-close; email flow also confirmed to render apollo-hero-gif-barking for Barking state per iter17. Two minor observations (non-blocking): (a) MOCKED asset — /app/frontend/assets/images/apollo-growling.gif is byte-identical (same md5 649092843bac042ff107b626348ed867) to /app/frontend/assets/images/apollo-barking.gif, so the growling animation visually renders the same frames as barking though the testID and file name are distinct; (b) expo-image on web does not forward accessibilityLabel to aria-label on the element (aria-label observed as null for the growling image); the testID selector still works reliably.

react_native_issues.issue: accessibilityLabel prop ('Apollo growling', 'Apollo barking', 'Apollo patrolling') is not forwarded to aria-label attribute on the rendered in the web preview by expo-image. Screen-reader labeling on the web target is therefore lost. testID-based e2e selection is unaffected. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/ApolloHero.tsx:109-115

action_items: MOCKED ASSET (main agent): /app/frontend/assets/images/apollo-growling.gif is byte-identical to apollo-barking.gif (same md5 649092843bac042ff107b626348ed867). Replace with an actual growling-specific animation before shipping so the visual differentiates growling (elevated suspicion) from barking (confirmed threat). Functional testID (apollo-hero-gif-growling) and accessibilityLabel ('Apollo growling') are already wired correctly.

MINOR (main agent, optional): expo-image on web target does not surface accessibilityLabel as aria-label. Either wrap the <Image> in a View with accessibilityLabel + accessible=true, or supply an explicit alt via the web-specific 'alt' prop on the Image, so assistive tech on the web preview reads the state.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/components/ApolloHero.tsx:108-116 — the state-to-gif mapping is a chain of ternaries with (state === 'barking' || state === 'biting') both mapping to apollo-hero-gif-barking. This means the 'biting' state renders the barking asset — intentional per iter17 but worth documenting; a small STATE_GIF constant map would make this data-driven and safer if more states get their own animations later.
/app/frontend/assets/images/apollo-growling.gif is a duplicate of apollo-barking.gif — this is a placeholder that must be replaced with a real growling animation before release.
